content.thinking:
I'm planning the qilin's design in full before writing anything: a deer-like body with green scales, cream chest and belly, gold antlers, cloud-like mane and tail, gold hooves and trim, and a jade pendant with tassels, sized like a tall slender horse around 1.4m body length.

Now I'm mapping out the skeleton — hips at the root, a spine chain built from a catmull path through hip, mid-body, and chest points, then a neck chain curving up from chest to head with multiple joints for smooth bending.

I attach the head joint to the last neck segment, angling it slightly forward and down, then add a jaw joint parented to the head positioned forward and below the head's center for the mouth.

Now I'm building the tail chain with a curved spline running back from the hips through several joints down to the tip, and starting a separate body sweep path running from behind the hips forward through the spine for the overall silhouette.

I'm shaping the body radius profile with a sine-based curve for the barrel, giving round caps at front and back and a fuller mid-section, with the belly line and chest positioned beneath the spine height.

For the neck and coat, I'm planning a dorsal green and cream belly color split using sectors, and considering wrapping a scale-pattern paint inside a cel shader so the scales pick up proper cel shading and shadow tones.

Now I'm working out countershading between the green scale paint and cream, nesting cel shading on both the green scales and a fainter cream scale texture for the belly.

For the legs I'm setting up inverted kinematics, defining shoulder and foot target positions and working through the upper leg, forearm, and cannon bone lengths to make sure they add up correctly to the shoulder height.

I'm adjusting the limb segment lengths so they bend naturally instead of staying nearly straight, and I'm figuring out the right number of named joints — shoulder, elbow, knee, fetlock — so the chain produces the correct number of spans plus a tip joint.

For the front leg, I'm setting lengths around 0.36, 0.34, 0.30, positioning the shoulder near the top and the fetlock near the ground, checking the reach distance stays under the total length so it bends properly. I'm working out where the elbow should bend forward slightly to match a deer's front leg anatomy.

For the hind leg, I'm placing the hip and target points, computing the segment lengths to sum slightly more than the distance so it bends naturally, with the stifle bending forward and the hock bending back to mimic a deer's hind leg joints.

For the leg tubes, I'm sweeping a tapered radius profile along each chain and setting up a color gradient—greenish scales on the upper leg transitioning to a darker teal/dark tone on the lower leg and foot.

Now I'm shaping the hoof as a cloven design with two separate toe pieces, positioning each as a small cylinder with distinct top/bottom radii, offsetting them along x with a slight z-scale stretch to form the split hoof look at the foot position.

I'm also adding a gold cuff band near the fetlock using a wider, flatter cylinder, and layering in soft cream-colored spheres as fur tufts at the fetlock back and knee for a fluffy texture.

For the gold armor pieces on the front legs, I'm planning simple gold ring cuffs at the carpus plus a small octahedron shape as a diamond accent on the cannon front, keeping it simpler than full plate geometry. Then I'm moving on to the head, positioning it at the end of the neck joint and building the skull from a scaled sphere oriented using the head's local forward/up directions.

Now I'm working out the muzzle as a swept capsule tapering toward the tip, with separate upper and lower jaw pieces -- the jaw hinges at a joint near the head and aims forward and down to form the mouth. I'm adding a dark gold nose sphere at the muzzle tip, tiny nostril spheres, and planning golden whisker sweeps curving back from the sides of the muzzle.

Now I'm placing amber iris eye decals on the skull using an azimuth-based positioning system, mirrored left and right, sizing them to fit proportionally on the roughly 0.2-wide head.

For the ears, I'm sketching a leaf-shaped outline extruded with smoothed edges to form deer-like ears, positioning them relative to the head's local coordinate frame.

I'll keep "left" consistently meaning +X for the model and use world X for absolute points. For ear color, I'll add a smaller pink inner extrude slightly thicker than the green outer one (0.011 vs 0.008) so it peeks through both faces.

For antlers, I'm plotting the main beam as a curve of points defined relative to the head's local frame, sweeping up, back, and then tipping forward near the top, keeping in mind the head's slight downward pitch when interpreting those directions.

Adding branch tines...

Now I'm thinking about the cloud-cream mane texture: placing cream spheres at brow and cheek positions, then considering swirl patterns for the neck mane using alternating cream and green spheres. I'm weighing whether to use sphere textures with a spiral decal or switch to flat circular cards with a spiral pattern instead, since sphere UV wrapping might not show the swirl cleanly.

I'm keeping colors distinct per texture - cream and green spiral strokes with a hand-drawn path approximating a swirl, rounded linecaps for a softer look. Then I'm planning the mane puffs along the neck, eight of them tapering in radius from withers to head.

For bone attachment, I realize I can just rely on the chain's automatic nearest-joint selection rather than manually computing offsets - simplifying things by letting the system pick the closest joint to each puff's position.

For the sphere geometry, I'll use a low-poly sphere with cel-shaded paint material, which gives a nice two-tone look based on world normals.

Now I'm planning the mane and tail puffs: shoulder and rump tufts, leg fluffs, and a cloud cluster of small cream and green spheres with swirl decals clustered at the raised tail tip, following a curving upward path.

For ornaments, I'm adding a gold chest sash as a loop swept around the body at the spine3 joint, making sure the loop logic picks the smallest ring around that point so it wraps the torso rather than catching the leg tubes nearby.

I'll place the loop frame slightly rearward using an explicit frame position and forward-facing normal rather than relying on nearest-bone placement, then build out a belly band in gold, possibly a second teal strap, plus a lathed jade medallion disc with a gold ring and tassels hanging from the chest.

For the medallion I need to find its front-facing position on the body surface: I'll try raycasting against the body mesh from a point above and in front, falling back to a manual coordinate guess if the ray misses, handling the nullable hit result safely. The medallion itself will be a gold torus shape.

Adding more jewelry parts...

Let me recalibrate body proportions: center y 1.0 with ry maxing at 0.25 gives belly at 0.75 and back at 1.25, which lines up with the shoulder joint. I'm positioning the front shoulder and hind hip joints, then working out leg segment lengths needed to reach a front foot target near ground level.

Now I'm reconsidering the spine path to curve upward slightly toward the chest, defining a sequence of points from hip to shoulder and adjusting the hip and chest positions to match this curve for the catmull spline.

For the bone weighting, since the hips and spine joints end up at nearly the same spline parameter, I'm figuring out which bone claims that overlapping segment — keeping it simple by letting the later-listed joint win and clamping the rear portion to the first span. Moving on to the neck now.

Trimming antlers to keep total height around 2.1m since the shoulder is horse-like at 1.27. For the neck I'm setting up cream-to-green color sectors and planning mane cloud puffs positioned along the neck's path with increasing offset and radius.

Now I'm adding more cloud wisps at the withers and hip, with a helper function that builds each puff as a sphere plus two side decals, working out the placement geometry so circles sit correctly on the curved surface.

Reducing segment count to 8 keeps triangle counts manageable for decals placed on puff surfaces, positioned and oriented relative to each puff's location. I'm also planning gradient tail clouds attached near tail joints, and starting to define the color palette with jade and teal tones for different body parts.

Filling out the rest of the palette with cream, gold, pink, and amber tones for ears and eyes. For gold flat parts I'll use cel-shaded paint instead of flat color since paints don't count toward the color limit, and I'm adding a subtle glow to the jade medallion and forehead gem for a bit of shimmer.

Writing scale paint definitions...

Adding more fur blend logic...

Adding dark nostrils, a thin cream lower jaw sweep, a chin beard spike, and two curved gold whisker sweeps flowing back from the muzzle using bezier paths with tapered radii...

For the eye area, I'm placing a decal on the skull sphere using an azimuth-based position around the skull center, accounting for the slight head pitch, then adding cream cheek puffs and a small green wisp near the ear base.

Now I'm defining the forelock tuft between the antlers and working out the antler geometry itself—a root point near the head with a sequence of offset points curving upward and forward, then branching into two separate antler tines with bezier curves for the tips.

Adding brow tine and gold rings...

Drawing the sash path from each shoulder down to the chest medallion, mirroring the left and right sides into a V shape with a thin flat gold ribbon and draping it onto the body with slight lift.

Now I'm adding a belly girth band around the waist, plus hip ornaments with pendants and tassels at each flank, using ray hits against the skin surface to position and orient the rings, jade discs, and tassel geometry correctly.

Still writing tassel geometry...

Now thinking about placing gold scroll ornaments on the rump, positioning them near the hip/thigh surface so they sit flush against the haunch rather than floating off the body.

Setting up leg radius tapers for front and hind legs, checking that leg groups fit within the body's silhouette, then sketching a cuff helper function that positions gold bands along leg segments using interpolation between joint points.

I'm adding a gold diamond-shaped plate on the cannon bone front surface, oriented along the leg segment direction, plus planning cream puff fluff spheres at the elbow and fetlock areas for texture detail.

Now I'm working out hoof bone assignments, figuring out that hooves should attach to the nearest bone segment automatically based on proximity to the tip joint rather than being explicitly assigned.

Still naming joints and setting parents...

Now I'm working out the tail geometry - sweeping a chain with tapering radii down to the tip, then placing cloud-puff decorations at various offsets near the tail's end to build that fluffy look.

For nearest-joint assignment, I'm sticking with the rule that each cloud attaches to whichever bone segment passes closest to it. Now I'm moving on to generating the mane puffs by stepping along the neck's path at regular intervals.

Checking part and triangle counts with decals included, I'm reducing decal segments to 6 to keep triangle totals manageable, landing around 130 parts total which stays well under budget. I'm also planning additional puff details like a withers tuft, forelock puffs, and a cream chest ruff near the front.

Staying within the 64-color budget since paints don't count against flats, I'm checking which imports and helpers I actually use to avoid strict unused-variable errors, and setting up a small vector helper plus swirl texture utilities for the cream stroke patterns.

Writing swirl paths...

Finishing the decal placement, then setting up cream and green painted materials for the puffs. Now I'm moving to the body surface with eyes, and setting up the leg chains using parent joints and arrays of points.

For limbs, I'm defining a signature that takes root, target, lengths, and bend directions so each joint curves the right way—elbows bending back, knees bending forward for the front legs, reversed for the hind legs to mimic a deer's natural stance. Then I'm setting up the three-segment IK for realistic leg articulation.

Checking the hind leg geometry: hip-to-target distance comes out to roughly 0.9, matching segment lengths of 0.4, 0.38, and 0.3. I'm also working out the hoof shape—sizing the cylinder and toe radii so they sit flush against the fetlock without overlapping awkwardly.

Overall height checks out around 2.1 meters including antler tip, reasonable for a tall qilin build. For the neck, I'm using a sweep function that tapers the radius from 0.115 down to 0.05 along its length for a smooth profile.

The neck chains off the last spine joint, and the head attaches at the neck's tip with a forward-downward tilt so it reads as naturally angled. I'll position the head's skull center slightly forward and up from where the neck ends.

Now I'm defining the jaw joint parented to the head, aimed forward-down, and sketching a tapered jaw bone with a cream-colored flat paint.

Next I'm shaping the upper snout as a tapered tube curving forward and slightly down from the head, with a cream base and a sector paint for coloring the dorsal side, then adding a dark nose sphere at the snout tip plus two tiny nostril spheres.

Now I'm placing jade fin-like ear frills at the cheeks, trying to build a leaf-shaped outline that sweeps backward without self-crossing.

Verifying the cheek fin shape is convex, then working out its placement and orientation relative to the head, computing the thickness direction from the cross product of its local axes.

Checking the ear plate orientation with similar cross-product logic for its thickness direction, then moving to add a gold chevron detail across the forehead.

Working out the gem's embedding depth on the ellipsoid surface, then adding a small gold torus ring around it facing upward, with a glow effect on the gem and starting on jade disc medallions.

For the neck, I'm sweeping a thin gold ring along the neck path using a frame at a point near the base, then considering a chest medallion placed via a ray cast onto the body surface to find the right attachment point.

Realizing the body's taper profile makes the front end too narrow for a deer's deep chest, I'm reworking the radius function so the chest bulges out around 80% along the body length instead of tapering symmetrically like a sine wave.

Checking the body path points and radius profile to figure out where the front end lands with the round cap added — trying to keep total body length around 1.3m, horse-like, with the neck emerging near z=0.3.

Working out path boundaries: rear cap at z=-0.68, front at z≈0.4, and placing the chest intersection point at roughly y=0.85, z=0.55 for the ray fallback. Spine chain knots run from hips at (0,1.0,-0.4) up toward the shoulder region, and the tail attaches at the rear tip z=-0.58, with the hind hip joint set near x=0.15, z=-0.42.

Now I'm positioning the front shoulder joint at z=0.28 and working out where the shoulder scroll spiral should sit relative to the body surface and front leg tube, aiming for the scroll center around x=0.215 so it floats just touching the torso.

Defining the spiral geometry parameters—turns, radius, axis orientation—then setting up a gold paint material and similarly placing a hip scroll on the opposite side, before moving to leg coloring with banded gradients along the chain.

Now I'm writing a per-leg generator function that computes root position, target foot position, and segment lengths based on whether it's a front or hind leg and which side of the body.

Writing cuff helper code...

Then I'm adding hock cuffs, upper leg fluff puffs, a greave diamond shape at the cannon front, cheap fur tufts using squashed cream spheres, a tassel helper combining bead, cone, and cap, and a couple chest ruff puffs — though I'm noting these might clash with the medallion placement.

Estimating total part count across body, mane, tail, back, chest, head puffs, legs, antlers, and tassels puts me around 350 parts, which feels manageable. Now I'm writing the mane generation loop, positioning puffs along the neck path with shrinking radius and alternating green/cream coloring.

Adding side puffs...

Now I'm starting the antler function, computing local offset points to build out the branching structure.

Still shaping the antler tines...

Now working out whisker curves with bezier sweeps from head to tips, then sketching a beard spike on the chin using the jaw bone.

Positioning the ears with inner pink outlines scaled down for depth, adding amber-colored iris eyes, and starting a ring-loop decoration around the body surface.

Adding gold studs along the ring path...

Now for the sash: I'm building a draped curve for the left side with a catmull path, then sweeping a tapering box-section strap along it for that diagonal fabric look.

For the chest medallion, I'm placing a torus-and-disc assembly at the hit point offset along the normal — gold torus ring with a jade cylinder disc centered on it as a small pendant helper function.

Adding a gold bead at the center and planning tassels hanging below, with small gold bead spheres plus cone shapes offset to either side.

Still writing imports...

Defining the skull geometry as a scaled sphere positioned relative to the head, then setting up the surface for attaching eyes and other facial details, with mirrored decal placement for symmetry.

I'm settling on a 2048 texture resolution for the paint sheet, balancing crispness for anime-style cel edges against texel density calculations across the model's surface area. Now I'm double-checking that leg and hip joint references are correctly ordered before finalizing the full code, with hooves positioned just above the floor plane.

Adding hoof geometry...

Then I'm adding fur tufts at the fetlocks and elbows for extra texture, placing small stretched spheres at each joint location. That should be everything needed, so I'm ready to write the final code.
